_comment: One entry per pass.
`source` is the recording: a .gpx of the road, or a .json Overpass
response for its OSM way. `./gen_tracks.py --survey` fetches the road and
writes that GPX itself, so the file does not have to exist yet — but a
recording you made by driving the road is better than anything a query
can produce, and if the file is there it is used as it stands.
`osm` says where to look: a bounding box (south, west, north, east), and
optionally a name or ref regex to narrow it. THESE BOXES ARE STARTING
POINTS, NOT SURVEY CONTROL. Draw the query at https://overpass-turbo.eu
and look at what it selects before trusting the import; a box that
catches the road on the other side of the valley measures that one just
as happily. `expect` is the cross-check: published figures for the road,
which the importer compares its measurement against and complains about.
`section` keeps one stretch, in metres from the start of the fetched way.
The real roads are 6-12km and a pass in the game is about 1.5km, which is
what its race pacing is built on. The geometry inside the section is
measured; where to start and stop is an authored choice, and it is
recorded in the track's real-world note.
`width` and `surface` are optional overrides. Leave them out and OSM tags
are used when present, falling back to a 6m mountain road on coarse
asphalt. `segment_names` is optional and positional; unnamed corners are
named after what they turned out to be.

tracks.name: Mt. Akina — Downhill
tracks.flavour: Five consecutive hairpins. The gutter is a line, if you're mad enough.
tracks.real_world: Mt. Haruna, Gunma — the east-face descent from Lake Haruna towards Takasaki.

tracks.name: Myogi — Uphill
tracks.flavour: Short, tight, and the crowd stands close enough to touch the mirrors.
tracks.real_world: Mt. Myogi, Gunma — the climb past the shrine on the Gunma side.

tracks.name: Irohazaka — One Way Down
tracks.flavour: Forty-eight corners, all numbered, all going the same direction. Down.
tracks.real_world: Iroha-zaka, Nikko, Tochigi — the descending one-way road.

tracks.name: Happogahara — High Speed
tracks.flavour: Wide, fast, and it rewards the brave over the clever.
tracks.real_world: Happogahara, Yaita, Tochigi — the road up onto the plateau.

tracks.name: Mt. Akagi — Downhill
tracks.flavour: Rhythm section after rhythm section. Break the rhythm, lose the race.
tracks.real_world: Mt. Akagi, Gunma — the descent on the south face from Lake Onuma.

tracks.name: Usui Pass — Downhill
tracks.flavour: Narrow, damp, and lined with a hundred and eighty corners of history.
tracks.real_world: Usui Pass, Gunma/Nagano — the old Route 18 between Yokokawa and Karuizawa. Published descriptions give 184 corners over about 11km and roughly 550m of elevation.
